Configuring the Cache

The Acme server keeps a cache of rendered pages in memory so that repeated requests are answered without running the template engine again. This guide explains how to size the cache, how entries expire, and how to clear it during deployments.

Cache size

Set the maximum size with the cache.maxEntries option. When the cache is full, the least recently used entry is evicted first. A good starting point is ten thousand entries, which uses roughly two hundred megabytes of memory for typical pages.

cache:
  maxEntries: 10000
  ttlSeconds: 300

Expiration

Each entry expires after ttlSeconds. Expired entries are removed lazily, the next time they are requested, so memory is not reclaimed immediately. Set the time to live to zero to disable expiration entirely.

Stale content

When the origin is slow, the server can serve stale entries for a short grace period while it refreshes them in the background. Enable this with cache.serveStale.

Clearing the cache

Run the acme cache clear command after each deployment, or send a POST request to the admin endpoint. Clearing the cache causes a brief spike in CPU usage while pages are rendered again.

OptionDefaultDescription
maxEntries1000Maximum number of cached pages
ttlSeconds60Lifetime of an entry in seconds
serveStalefalseServe expired entries while refreshing
